ET-M3-1.statement: Generation runs only from known sim scenes, with the initial state and asset hashes saved first; a scene-consistency check rejects injected mismatches.
ET-M3-1.candidate: a candidate is (i) a candidate manifest: the snapshot manifest's task id and version, seed, asset sha256s, cube half size and colour, and goal position; and (ii) frames 0 to T of one recorded episode on that scene, rendered at 512 x 512 from the human render camera, frame 0 after restore_state and frame t after control step t. No generator exists yet, so physics frames stand in for generated frames.
ET-M3-1.episode_kind: on even seeds the nominal scripted demo (VARIANTS['nominal']); on odd seeds an operator episode, m3-synth-lateral-miss and m3-synth-close-high alternating by seed, drawn as F2's rule below
ET-M3-1.tolerance_pilot: block 10 seeds 10900 to 10919, used for nothing else, with the same nominal and operator alternation. The checker's mask rules (red: R > 120, G < 60, B < 60; green: G > 120, R < 80, B < 80; 8-connectivity), the cube area band [a_lo, a_hi], the merge radius for red components, the first-frame tolerance and the goal-centroid distance are set from the pilot: each tolerance is the pilot's observed extreme widened by 10%, the band subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56 so that the 0.6 and 1.6 resizes stay outside it. They are written to evals/M3-checker-tolerances.json, whose sha256 is recorded in the status ledger before any control or injection is generated. If no such band contains every pilot frame, the owner is told before any candidate is generated.
ET-M3-1.controls: 60 unmodified candidates on block 10 seeds 10000 to 10059
ET-M3-1.injections: 10 of each of six types, seed = 10100 + 10 x (t - 1) + i for type t = 1 to 6 and i = 0 to 9, each injected into its own unmodified source candidate on that seed. rng = random.Random(seed); its first draw is the injection step, rng.randrange(1, T), so frame 0 is never altered by a frame injection; further draws follow in the order below. A frame injection alters that frame and every later one. (1) object removed: in each altered frame, every pixel of the cube's red mask is replaced by the per-channel median of the non-red, non-green pixels in the ring 1 to 6 px outside the mask's bounding box, or 6 to 12 px if that ring has fewer than 20 such pixels. (2) object duplicated: the cube's masked pixels copied unchanged to the first offset in [(0, +60), (0, -60), (+60, 0), (-60, 0), (+60, +60), (-60, -60)] px (row, column) whose destination bounding box lies in the image and holds no red or green pixel in the injection frame; that offset is kept for later frames. (3) cube resized: factor rng.choice([0.6, 1.6]); the cube removed as in (1), then its bounding-box patch resized by nearest neighbour about the mask's centroid and only the resized mask's pixels pasted. (4) goal or task changed, by i: i in {0, 3, 6, 9}: the manifest's goal position moved by rng.uniform(0.03, 0.06) m along angle rng.uniform(0, 2 pi) in xy; i in {1, 4, 7}: the manifest's task id set to 'PickCube-v1' or its version changed; i in {2, 5, 8}: the green goal pixels in every altered frame shifted by the image displacement of a rng.uniform(0.03, 0.06) m goal move, computed from the camera's projection, with the manifest unchanged. (5) asset hash broken: in the manifest, the asset sha256 at index rng.randrange(n_assets) has its first hex digit replaced by a different one. (6) initial render mismatch: frame 0 replaced by the snapshot render of seed + 500, rendered for this purpose only.
ET-M3-1.checker: deterministic, with no learned part: the candidate manifest's fields equal the snapshot's; frame 0 equals the snapshot's saved render within the first-frame tolerance; in every frame, the red components within the merge radius of the largest one's centroid together have an area within [a_lo, a_hi] x the snapshot render's cube area, and no other red component of at least 0.25 x that area exists; and the green goal pixels' centroid is within the goal-centroid distance of the snapshot's, in frames with at least the pilot's minimum count of green pixels.
ET-M3-1.threshold: 100% of the 60 injected candidates rejected, an injection counting as rejected only when its unmodified source candidate passes every check and the injected one fails at least one (an injection whose source fails counts as not rejected); and at most 3 of the 60 controls (5%) falsely rejected
ET-M3-1.if_it_fails: recorded as failed. A revised checker needs m3-protocol-2, a new tolerance pilot on block 10 seeds 10300 to 10319, and fresh controls and injections on new seeds
ET-M3-1.reported: rejections by type and by the check that caught each; every source candidate's own result; false rejections with their cause; the false-rejection count with its Wilson 95% interval; and a statement that controls are physics renders, so this does not estimate false rejection on generated frames (ET-M3-2 measures that)

ET-M3-2.threshold: false acceptance <= 10% on >= 100 audited accepted candidates, with >= 50 rejected candidates also audited (design section 1), decided on the point estimate with the Wilson interval reported (owner D6)

ET-M3-3.threshold: the generated-data arm beats ordinary augmentation by >= 5 points of success, pooled over >= 3 seeds, with the paired 95% interval's lower bound above 0 (owner D6)

ET-M3-6.statement: Targeted synthetic failure data improves prediction on a failure family held out from training.
ET-M3-6.target: m0-scripted-missed-grasp, chosen by evals/M3-remeasure.json's rule (reports/WO-020-m3-remeasure-family-gaps.md): its worst value under plain A is the joints at horizon 1, -62.9%
ET-M3-6.model: WO-004's: carry-contact-beta-fall trained 30 epochs, seeds 0, 1 and 2, every hyperparameter as in runs/20261102T041509Z_93dd348c, evaluated as the 3-member ensemble mean with plain A (carry-contact-beta-fall-still-reach) and the predicted flag
ET-M3-6.base_training: M0's train partition minus all 30 m0-scripted-missed-grasp episodes and minus the 23 episodes with seed divisible by 10 of the other six families, which are the no-harm holdout and are never trained on: a 207-episode base fit set, 31,031 windows (WINDOW 14, stride 1). This departs from the design's 230 (WO-014) so that one model per arm serves both the evaluation family and the no-harm check; F0's numbers are therefore not expected to equal WO-020's. Any run whose counts differ stops before training.
ET-M3-6.normalization: every arm uses the statistics compute_pilot._Data computes on the 207-episode base fit set (state_mean, state_std, delta_std, lag, action_mean, action_std), unchanged; the five baselines on the no-harm holdout and on the evaluation family are computed once with those statistics and shared by every arm. An arm's training windows are the base fit windows in manifest order, then its added windows in the order they were drawn or generated.

arms.F_star: base plus the 27 m0-scripted-missed-grasp train episodes whose seed is not divisible by 10, so that base plus F_star is WO-004's 234-episode seed-holdout fit set; they add W* = 4,161 windows. The reference arm: it never counts toward a pass.
arms.F1: base plus a fixed set of W* augmented windows, drawn once and shared by all seeds: rng = numpy.random.default_rng(1); idx = rng.integers(0, 31031, 4161); the conditioning states (window steps 0 to 3, joint_position and object_position only) get rng.normal noise of sd 0.05 x that dimension's base state_std, and every action gets rng.normal noise of sd 0.05 x the base action_std, independent per element, in that order; target states (steps 4 to 13), target_position and object_grasped are unchanged
arms.F2: base plus operator episodes from physics, recorded on block 11 scenes in ascending seed order from 11000, skipping (and listing) scenes that fail the reproducibility gate, one episode per scene, operators alternating lateral-miss, close-high, lateral-miss, and so on. Episode parameters come from random.Random(seed).uniform: m3-synth-lateral-miss uses PlanSettings(grasp_offset_xy_m=(0.0, s x d)), d in [0.02, 0.05] m, s = +1 for the 1st, 3rd, 5th lateral-miss episode and -1 for the 2nd, 4th, 6th; m3-synth-close-high uses PlanSettings(grasp_height_m=0.012 + d), d in [0.02, 0.04] m; every other setting at its default; ScriptedPickPlace with noise_seed = seed. Every recorded episode is kept whatever its rubric label (labels reported). Episodes are added in order until their windows reach W*, and windows of the last episode past W* are dropped from its end, so the arm adds exactly W* windows.
arms.F1s: reported only, not in the threshold: base plus the nominal scripted demos of F2's own scenes, in F2's order, truncated to W* windows, to separate new-scene diversity from failure targeting
arms.F3: Pipeline A: M2a's observation model generates observations for F2's exact scenes and operator actions, in F2's order. Only candidates the filter accepts are kept; each rejected one is replaced by the next operator episode drawn by F2's rule, until accepted windows reach W* or 3 x F2's episode count candidates have been generated. If Pipeline A's model does not exist when F3's work order starts, F3 uses Pipeline B through its replay variant (design section 2, step 6), and that choice is recorded in the status ledger before any F3 candidate is generated. If accepted windows stay below W*, F3 is trained on what was accepted, reported as unmatched, and ET-M3-6 is not passed.

ET-M3-6.evaluation_family: m3-eval-missed-grasp: block 16 seeds in ascending order from 16000, with exactly m0-scripted-missed-grasp's PlanSettings, until 60 episodes pass the reproducibility gate, which replays each evaluation episode itself (at most seeds 16000 to 16099; skipped seeds listed). Planning failures are kept. Episode id m3-eval-missed-grasp-seed-<seed:06d>, scene_group_id m3-seed-block-16. Recorded once, after this freeze and before any arm is trained; nobody inspects its trajectories or metrics before scoring.
ET-M3-6.metric: on the evaluation family, over all its stride-1 windows: each required stream's RMSE in own units (joint_position in rad, object_position in m) at each horizon 1 to 10, per seed, of the ensemble mean under plain A with the predicted flag
ET-M3-6.helps_rule: Arm Fk helps when (a) for every seed s in {0, 1, 2}, horizon h in 1 to 10 and stream in {joint_position, object_position}: RMSE(Fk, s, h, stream) < RMSE(F1, s, h, stream) strictly, values equal to 6 significant figures counting as not below; and (b) W(Fk) >= W(F0) - 0.02, where W is the minimum over seeds, horizons and both streams of 1 - RMSE_model / RMSE of the lowest of the five baselines, on the 23 no-harm episodes
ET-M3-6.threshold: ET-M3-6 passes if F3 helps by the rule. F2 against F1 says whether added physics failure data helps; F2 against F1s whether targeting failures helps beyond new nominal scenes. Both are reported whatever F3 shows; F2 is never reported as generated data (owner D8).
ET-M3-6.sensitivity: F_star is scored by the helps rule against F1 and reported with ET-M3-6. If F_star does not help, ET-M3-6's result is still F3's by the rule, but it is reported as 'the rule could not detect help even from collected target data'.
ET-M3-6.reported: every arm's RMSE table, and per seed both streams' F1 - Fk differences at every horizon; the fraction of the gap closed, (F0 - Fk) / (F0 - F_star), per stream and seed at horizons 1 and 10, 'undefined' where F0 - F_star <= 0; each arm's training windows and episodes
ET-M3-6.scored_once: each arm is trained once per seed and scored once on the evaluation family; nothing is tuned on it. F3's generator, its training data, its filter tolerances, its candidate list and count are frozen with ET-M3-2's protocol before F3 is trained, and nothing in them is chosen from any arm's evaluation-family or no-harm result; that protocol states which arms' results were known when it was frozen.

not_frozen_here: ET-M3-2, ET-M3-3, ET-M3-4 and ET-M3-5's full protocols, before their own work orders
